name: Duene
prior: The idea's 'Nichts im Markt' is false since September 2026: Vald Labs KURARE is a polyphonic synthesizer 'inspired by the Kuramoto model of collective synchronisation', POPULATE up to 32 oscillators per swarm, DECOUPLE (tight sync -> drifting clouds), DIVERGE, EXCITE, 16 voices, two swarms per note, public beta 0.5.0 for macOS/Windows, iOS planned (VS: matrixsynth.com/2026/09/vald-labs-kurare-every-note-is-crowd.html; sonicstate.com/news/2026/09/23/new-synths-from-vald-labs-). Chiral Audio Foxfire: a 16-voice Kuramoto chorus effect whose Coupling control runs from drift through 'flicker at the critical point' to lock (VS: kvraudio.com/product/foxfire-by-chiral-audio; rekkerd.org chiral-audio-launches-effect-plugins-defined-by-real-equations). Niche/academic: aleks.ksync Max abstraction (VS: github.com/aleksati/aleks.max), Nolan Lem Kuroscillators (SMC 2019, VS: smc2019.uma.es P3_09), 'Kuramoto drone' browser piece (VS: mi.wrocenter.pl/en/kuramoto-drone), Moon NIME 2024 Kuramoto vs Janus (VS: nime.org/proc/nime2024_60), Ling 'Synchronized Synthesis' MATLAB (VS: mathworks.com fileexchange/92588). Dune physics: Douady et al., 'The song of the dunes as a self-synchronized instrument', PRL 2006 - frequency equals the grains' relative-motion frequency, sound because moving grains synchronise, 65-110 Hz, lab reproduction without a dune (VS: arxiv.org/pdf/nlin/0412047; labo.msc.u-paris.fr/~daerr/reprints/Douady-et-al_Song-dunes_PRL2006.pdf); mechanism still debated, Dagois-Bohy et al. 2010 shear-plug instability (VS: physicsworld.com/a/the-troubled-song-of-the-sand-dunes). Distinction that remains: KURARE and Foxfire synchronise waveform oscillators (a unison that locks); Duene synchronises collision impulses so that the existence of a pitch is the transition from noise to tone, with a sand-bed body and a Puls gate deciding whether a slide catches - not found as such. See also designer-dun.json (same conclusion, different DSP).
costNotes: Worklet only (16 coupled phases with a mean field, impulses into resonators). Measured (M: sim/eng_min5.js, eng_dun_cost.js, eng_dun_cost2.js; Node 22 x64, shared Xeon, min of 5, noisy +-40 %): N = 16, coupling every 8 samples, 2 resonators + noise = 72 ns/sample min (72-120 across runs) = 0.6-0.9 units; N = 48 = 205-250 ns = 1.7-2.1 units. The sub-rate of the coupling is NOT the bottleneck (P = 32 did not help; the 16 per-sample phase increments + wrap tests in a Float64Array cost ~4-5 ns each, as webaudio.md section 3 warns for typed-array state); a phase-major block loop (per phase over 128 samples into an impulse buffer) did not help either in this bench. Realistic floor ~50 ns with cycles-instead-of-radians phases (wrap at 1.0) and Float32 -> ~0.5. With node 0.06 + 3 params 0.09: ~0.8 at level 1 (idea's 0.5 is 1.5x optimistic), level 3 with N = 48 ~2.0 (idea 1.2) - use N = 32 (~1.3) or 2 x 16 split L/R. The mean field needs sqrt + atan2 every 8 samples (~10 ns amortised) - fine. Phone x1.0-1.5.
soundHeld: Lock-in is fast, not slow: at f = 100 Hz, sigma 0.1, N = 16, K = 1.5 x (2 sigma omega) the order parameter r goes 0.2 -> 0.98 inside the first 50 ms; K = 0.7 x -> 0.9 within 100 ms; K = 0.5 x leaves r fluctuating 0.2-0.7 (the critical zone); f = 55 Hz locks within ~100 ms; f = 1000 Hz with coupling every 32 samples locks within 50 ms (M). The idea's risk 'Einrastzeit > 2 s' only applies within a few percent of Kc. The consequence is the opposite danger: with a linear K(y) the finger is an on/off switch - the rich flickering band (r 0.2-0.7) occupies a thin slice of y around 0.5-0.7 Kc. K(y) must be mapped so that most of the finger travel lies in 0.3-1.0 Kc (log or soft curve, with Kc estimated from sigma and f per note, since Kc scales with f). Fully locked (r >= 0.95) is a jittered pulse train = buzzy above ~250-300 Hz; dunes boom at 65-110 Hz, so the instrument's range should be ~30-250 Hz with 2-3 sand-bed resonators and a lowpass, and the finite-N fluctuations (1/sqrt(16) = 0.25) plus +-5 % impulse jitter keep the locked tone from being sterile. The noise -> tone transition on a held low note under a slow Hoehe is genuinely new in a touch instrument; first-order Kuramoto has no hysteresis, so the 'moment' is a soft crossover, not a snap (A; designer-dun.json says the same) - an adaptive K or inertia term would add bistability at ~10 % more cost.
soundBurst: Holds up (M): because lock takes 1-10 cycles, a 60-100 ms Puls gate at 100 Hz does catch (tone) when K >= Kc and does not when K < Kc, and at 55 Hz a 50-ms gate does not - the gate length and the lane's Kopplung decide hiss vs boom, exactly the 'Rutschung rastet ein oder nicht' the idea sells. Dephasing at K = 0 from a coherent start takes ~50 ms (r 1 -> 0.3; M), so phases kept between hits do not carry much coherence at 1/8 or slower - fine. The inverted burst (coherent start, K below Kc: a boom that crumbles to sand over the decay) is the better default for short gates and keeps pitch at the onset.
failureModes: Cost 0.8 (measured core 0.6-0.9), not 0.5; N = 48 at level 3 is ~2 units - use 32 or 2 x 16
Linear K(y) makes the finger a switch: lock-in is tens of ms, the flickering band is a thin slice of K - needs a nonlinear K(y) around a per-note Kc
Locked state = buzzy pulse train above ~250 Hz; keep the range low and the sand bed dark, or it is a rough Koerner
No hysteresis in first-order Kuramoto - the 'moment' is a crossfade (A)
Name and image clash with Koerner (Sandkoerner) - the untertitle 'Sand' does not fix that in a list; consider the subtitle 'Singender Sand'
Per-sample typed-array phase loop is the cost driver; must be written with locals/Float32/cycles and benchmarked in the real worklet before VCOST entry
Worklet thread move at first load; exceptions in process() silence the voice (R: webaudio.md sections 2-3) - clamp phases and r

KURARE (2026) and Foxfire are now the reference points for 'Kuramoto synth' - the release text must say what is different (impulses, noise -> pitch, sand body), or reviewers will call it a KURARE clone
verdict: Rare, and the idea's novelty claim needs correcting: Vald Labs KURARE (Sept 2026, a polyphonic Kuramoto swarm synth with up to 32 oscillators per swarm) and Chiral Audio Foxfire (Kuramoto chorus) exist, plus Max/MATLAB/NIME work; what is still unfound is pitch emerging from synchronised collision impulses with a sand body and a gate that decides whether a slide catches. Worklet; measured core 0.6-0.9 units for N = 16 (phase loop, not the coupling, is the cost), so ~0.8 at level 1 and ~2.0 at N = 48 - trim level 3 to 32. The simulation overturns the stated risk: lock-in takes 50-100 ms, not seconds, so the Puls gesture works, but a linear K(y) turns the held note into a switch - the mapping must be curved around a per-note Kc to keep the finger in the flickering band, and the range must stay below ~250 Hz or the locked tone is a buzz. Build it with those two fixes.
